candidates.original_title: Timing of Antiretroviral Therapy for HIV-1 Infection and Tuberculosis
candidates.description: Earlier ART initiation (within 2 weeks of TB treatment initiation) reduces the rate of new AIDS defining illness or death in HIV-TB co-infected patients with CD4 counts less than 50 compared with later ART initiation (between 8 and 12 weeks after TB treatment initiation)
candidates.citation_sentence: Havlir et al., used for this replication, was a large multisite trial conducted in 26 countries.
candidates.notes: The pure replication largely confirmed the original findings (similar p-values and proportions for most subgroups), but the MEA (ANCOVA, IV) weakened the main results. The authors' own conclusion is hedging: 'the results of this replication do not provide strong support that earlier ART initiation reduces the rate of new AIDS events.' A second coder might classify this as failure given the authors' conclusion, or as success based on the pure replication alone, hence ambiguous. The pure replication finds p=0.02 for CD4<50 (matching original), but ANCOVA reduces significance to p=0.066 and IV analysis shows no effect for CD4<50. Authors hedge: 'do not provide strong support.' The paper's reference [5] gives DOI as a supplement file URL; the article DOI 10.1056/NEJMoa1013607 is used instead.
